historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Significant divergence: EPS declining sharply (-9.5% 5yr CAGR, -17.3% 3yr) while revenue is roughly flat (-0.2%). Reflects severe margin compression and elevated D&A/financing during the SPK-30 transformation. FCF is the most reliable driver for a mature telco; the base case assumes broadly flat-to-mildly-declining FCF as cost-out ($51m delivered in H1 FY26, $110-140m annualised target by FY27) offsets low-single-digit revenue erosion.

base.rationale: Mature, ex-growth NZ telco. FY26 FCF guidance $290-330m (reaffirmed at H1). Cost-out offsets revenue decline to keep FCF broadly flat; terminal growth 1.5% (below NZ long-run GDP) for a structurally challenged incumbent.

bull.rationale: Mobile service revenue momentum (+1.6% H1 FY26, ARPU +5% in highest-value segment) sustains, full $110-140m cost-out lands, deleveraging to ~1.7x lowers financing drag, and the 25% data-centre stake adds optionality.

bear.rationale: Competition and enterprise/government structural decline accelerate, cost-out stalls against organisational disruption, dividend pressure persists, and the FCF base erodes.

valuation_philosophy: Spark is a mature, ex-growth NZ telco incumbent in structural decline, valued primarily on its free-cash-flow generation and dividend rather than growth. The DCF deliberately uses broadly flat-to-declining FCF (FY25 $330m, FY26 guidance $290-330m reaffirmed at H1) because revenue has been flat-to-down for five years (-0.2% 5yr CAGR) while EPS has fallen sharply (-9.5% 5yr) on margin compression. The base-case intrinsic value of $1.42 sits below the current price of $1.875, consistent with a stock that has de-rated ~60% from its FY23 peak (~$5.40) as the market re-priced the earnings downgrades and the 36% interim dividend cut (8.0 cps in H1 FY26 vs 12.5 cps). For income investors the thesis is now yield-plus-deleveraging: the new FCF-linked dividend policy (70-100% of FCF) supports a still-attractive trailing yield, but the payout is funded by a shrinking FCF base, so capital appreciation requires the SPK-30 cost-out program and mobile momentum (H1 FY26: mobile service revenue +1.6%, EBITDAI +10% reported, FCF +84.5%) to durably stabilise earnings.

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. The base-case IV ($1.42) implies P/E 11.5x, P/B 1.81x and EV/EBITDA 3.9x on FY25 actuals - all well below the 10-year historical averages (P/E 21.2x, EV/EBITDA 8.5x). The DCF is conservative, not over-valued: base upside is negative (-24%) and the current price sits in the lower half of the 10yr range (1.87 vs ~1.87-5.40). This is the opposite of the SEK.NZ peak-extrapolation failure mode. No fix required.
